references.text: The question about paying taxes to the emperor recalls David's census of the people, which also involved a form of taxation or registration that was viewed with suspicion.
Jesus discusses the earlier payment of temple tax, showing his attitude toward taxes and levies.
Luke's parallel account of the incident regarding taxes to the emperor, emphasizing the question of loyalty to God versus the emperor.
Mark's version of the event, which also explores the theme of giving to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.
The call to obey authorities because they are established by God can be seen in connection with the discussion about paying taxes to the emperor.
